newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE coffee rebounds from lows on roaster buying.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE coffee rebounds from lows on roaster buying.

text.p: Except for spot March, LIFFE robusta coffee futures rebounded from their lows to end Friday at day's peak on late short-covering but the market still failed to erase earlier sharp losses.
"There's more physical interest today for robustas. That's why robustas perform better towards the end of the day," said one trader. "The lower (price) levels attracted the industry buying."

By the finish, May was just $1 down at $1,729 a tonne after a session low of $1,670. July remained traded at par with May but March failed to recover from earlier low of $1,690 to end $52 off at $1,695.
New York's May arabica futures were down but May was still flirting with $1.90 a lb level.

It moved toward the morning high of 193.50 cents as the market found strength on news German statistician F.O. Licht lowered forecast of world 1996/97 coffee crop to 95.6 million bags from its earlier estimate of 97.7 million, one U.S. trader said.
News African robusta producers agreed to cut first half 1997 exports by 850,000 bags with Ivory Coast taking a 29 percent cut was within earlier trade expectation and had no immediate influence.

The market also found little support from comments by Brazil's Febec official that Brazil's exports between January and June this year was unlikely to exceed six million bag quota originally set by other producer nations. -- Jalil Hamid, London newsroom +44 171 542 4985
